akhfash:1-1.t: [He said] ﴿قُلْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ ٱسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ﴾: the alif of ﴿أَنه﴾ has fatḥa because it is a noun. «[Translator's note: i.e., the clause stands in the position of a noun, the deputy agent of أُوحِيَ.]» Then He said ﴿وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا﴾ [3]: (with kasra) as a fresh beginning, since it is part of the speech of the jinn; and whoever reads it with fatḥa makes it dependent on "revelation" (الوحي), and that is good. «[Translator's note: the quotation of verse 3 is printed with fatḥa in the source, though the author is describing the reading with kasra, إِنَّهُ.]»

akhfash:8-8.t: And He said ﴿وَشُهُباً﴾; its singular is الشِّهاب (a shooting flame).

akhfash:17-17.t: And He said ﴿لِّنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ because you say "فَتَنْتُه" ("I tried him"), and some Arabs say "أَفْتُنُه"; so that (form) follows that dialect. «[Translator's note: so in the source; the dialectal form meant is presumably the Form IV أَفْتَنْتُه.]»

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿أُوحِيَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ﴾ anna and its noun, and a past verb. ﴿نَفَرٌ﴾ its fāʿil. ﴿مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of نفر; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from anna, its noun and its predicate is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of أوحي; the clause «أوحي..» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَقالُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause استمع. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿سَمِعْنا قُرْآناً﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿عَجَباً﴾ an adjective; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿يَهْدِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿إِلَى الرُّشْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is a second adjective (ṣifa) of قرآنا. ﴿فَآمَنَّا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَلَنْ نُشْرِكَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan, whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِرَبِّنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿أَحَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is also conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and anna and its noun. ﴿تَعالى جَدُّ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), i.e. He is exalted above what is ascribed to Him. ﴿رَبِّنا﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿مَا اتَّخَذَ﴾ mā is negative, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿صاحِبَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَلا وَلَداً﴾ conjoined to صاحبة; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ كانَ﴾ anna and its noun, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir). ﴿يَقُولُ سَفِيهُنا﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and the clause of kāna is the khabar of anna, and the clause أنه is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يقول. ﴿شَطَطاً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْ لَنْ تَقُولَ﴾ an is lightened (mukhaffafa), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan. ﴿الْإِنْسُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿وَالْجِنُّ﴾ conjoined to الإنس. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿كَذِباً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause لن تقول is the khabar of the lightened an, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from the lightened an, its noun and its predicate stands in place of the two objects of ظننا.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ كانَ رِجالٌ﴾ anna and its noun, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun. ﴿مِنَ الْإِنْسِ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of رجال. ﴿يَعُوذُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and the clause of kāna is the khabar of أنه, and the clause أنه is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿بِرِجالٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يعوذون. ﴿مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ an adjective of رجال. ﴿فَزادُوهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿رَهَقاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُمْ ظَنُّوا﴾ anna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of أنهم, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿كَما﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿ظَنَنْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿أَنْ﴾ an, lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). ﴿لَنْ يَبْعَثَ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil. ﴿أَحَداً﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar of an, and the maṣdar formed from the lightened an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of ظن.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿لَمَسْنَا السَّماءَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَوَجَدْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مُلِئَتْ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿حَرَساً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿شَدِيداً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of حرسا. ﴿وَشُهُباً﴾ conjoined to حرسا; the clause ملئت is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا كُنَّا﴾ anna and its noun, and kāna and its noun. ﴿نَقْعُدُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كنا, and the clause كنا is the khabar of أنا, and the clause أنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مَقاعِدَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿لِلسَّمْعِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb نقعد. ﴿فَمَنْ يَسْتَمِعِ﴾ man is a conditional noun that makes jussive, as mubtadaʾ (subject), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿الْآنَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿يَجِدْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿شِهاباً﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿رَصَداً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of شهابا; the clause يجد is the apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause of من is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿لا نَدْرِي﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of أنا, and the clause أنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿أَشَرٌّ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation. ﴿شَرٌّ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb. ﴿أُرِيدَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِمَنْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the clause أريد is explicative (mufassira), with no grammatical position, and the clause أشر stands in place of the two objects of ندري. ﴿أَمْ أَرادَ﴾ a conjunction and a past verb. ﴿بِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿رَبُّهُمْ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿رَشَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿مِنَّا﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿الصَّالِحُونَ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the khabar of أنا, and the clause أنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَمِنَّا﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿دُونَ﴾ an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) a postponed mubtadaʾ, according to Ibn Hishām in al-Shudhūr. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كُنَّا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿طَرائِقَ﴾ its khabar. ﴿قِدَداً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of طرائق; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of أنا, and the clause أنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْ﴾ an, lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). ﴿لَنْ نُعْجِزَ اللَّهَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the Name of Majesty is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar of the lightened an. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the interpreted maṣdar formed from the lightened an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of ظننا. ﴿وَلَنْ نُعْجِزَهُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿هَرَباً﴾ ḥāl.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive. ﴿سَمِعْنَا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْهُدى﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿آمَنَّا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position, and lammā with what it governs is the khabar (predicate) of أنا, and the clause أنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿من﴾ a conditional noun that makes jussive, as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُؤْمِنْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِرَبِّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa). ﴿لا يَخافُ﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause of من is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بَخْساً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿رَهَقاً﴾ conjoined to بخسا; its meaning is: injustice.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿مِنَّا﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿الْمُسْلِمُونَ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the khabar of أنا, and the clause أنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَمِنَّا الْقاسِطُونَ﴾ conjoined to its like; القاسطون means: those who deviate unjustly through their disbelief. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿من﴾ a conditional noun that makes jussive, as mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَسْلَمَ﴾ a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿فَأُولئِكَ تَحَرَّوْا﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and a demonstrative as mubtadaʾ, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar of أولئك. ﴿رَشَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause أولئك is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause of من is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:15-15.t: [Translator's note: the quotation marks and the beginnings of the Quranic words are corrupted in the source here («َ أَمَّا» … «مَّا» … «لْقاسِطُونَ» … «َكانُوا» … «ِجَهَنَّمَ» … «َ طَباً»); the words are restored below from the verse وَأَمَّا الْقاسِطُونَ فَكانُوا لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَباً.] «وَأَمَّا» the wāw is a resumptive particle. «أمّا» a particle of condition and detailing (sharṭ wa-tafṣīl). «الْقاسِطُونَ» mubtadaʾ (subject). «فَكانُوا» the fāʾ occurring in the apodosis of the condition, and kāna and its noun. «لِجَهَنَّمَ» a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial). «حَطَباً» khabar (predicate) of كانوا; the clause كانوا is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause «أما القاسطون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ﴾ an, lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). ﴿لَوِ﴾ conditional, not making jussive. ﴿اسْتَقامُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿لَأَسْقَيْناهُمْ﴾ the lām occurring in the apodosis of the condition, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ماءً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿غَدَقاً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of ماء; its meaning is: abundant. The clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position, and the condition and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of an, and the clause of an is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb أسقيناهم. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a conditional noun that makes jussive, as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُعْرِضْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm). ﴿عَنْ ذِكْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يعرض. ﴿رَبِّهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يَسْلُكْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَذاباً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿صَعَداً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of عذابا; the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of من, and the clause «من..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ﴾ anna and its noun; and ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of anna; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) [Translator's note: the verb تدعوا is not quoted in the source]; and ﴿مَعَ اللَّهِ﴾ an adverb of place annexed to the Name of Majesty; and ﴿أَحَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿لَمَّا قامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ﴾ lammā is a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿يَدْعُوهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿كادُوا﴾ kāda and its noun. ﴿يَكُونُونَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its noun. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿لِبَداً﴾ khabar; the clause يكونون is the khabar of kāda, and the clause كادوا is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position, and lammā with what it governs is the khabar of أنه, and the clause «أنه..» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ a restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿أَدْعُوا﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿رَبِّي﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا أُشْرِكُ﴾ negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَحَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أدعو.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun; and ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿أَمْلِكُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿ضَرًّا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿رَشَداً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ضرا; the clause «لا أملك..» is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَنْ يُجِيرَنِي﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan, and the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the first person is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾ fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَلَنْ أَجِدَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the accusative by lan, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مُلْتَحَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿بَلاغاً﴾ excepted (mustathnā), accusative (manṣūb). ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) بلاغا. ﴿وَرِسالاتِهِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to بلاغا. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿مِنَ﴾ a conditional noun that makes jussive, as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; the word in the verse is مَن]. ﴿يَعْصِ اللَّهَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ conjoined to the Name of Majesty. ﴿فَإِنَّ﴾ the fāʾ occurring in the apodosis of the condition, and a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿نارَ﴾ the postponed noun of inna. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خالدين. ﴿أَبَداً﴾ an adverb of time; the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause «من..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of beginning (ḥarf ibtidāʾ); and ﴿إِذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive. ﴿رَأَوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation; and ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and the sīn of futurity, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿أَضْعَفُ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi, and the clause «سيعلمون..» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿ناصِراً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿وَأَقَلُّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أضعف. ﴿عَدَداً﴾ tamyīz.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative. ﴿أَدْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَقَرِيبٌ﴾ the hamza of interrogation; and ﴿قَرِيبٌ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate); and ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause stands in place of the two objects of أدري, and the clause «إن أدري..» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and ﴿تُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); and ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَجْعَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); and ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿رَبِّي﴾ fāʿil; and ﴿أَمَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿عالِمُ﴾ khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause «هو عالم» is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿الْغَيْبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُظْهِرُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿عَلى غَيْبِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿أَحَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and ﴿مَنِ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿ارْتَضى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿مِنْ رَسُولٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَإِنَّهُ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and inna and its noun. ﴿يَسْلُكُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿يَدَيْهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ both conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes them. ﴿رَصَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of من.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿لِيَعْلَمَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb يسلك; and ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); and ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). ﴿أَبْلَغُوا رِسالاتِ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the lightened an, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from the lightened an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يعلم. ﴿وَأَحاطَ﴾ the wāw is of ḥāl (circumstantial), and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ an adverb of place; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَأَحْصى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أحاط; and ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, annexed to ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَدَداً﴾ tamyīz (specification).

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أُوحِىَ إِلَىَّ﴾.
The readers are agreed [218/a] on (أُوحِىَ). Juwayya al-Asadī read it: "قُلْ أُحِىَ إِلَىَّ", from وحيتُ, putting a hamza for the wāw because it took a ḍamma, as He said: ﴿وإِذَا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ﴾.
His saying: ﴿ٱسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ﴾.
It is mentioned that when the devils were pelted and the sky was guarded against them, Iblīs said: This is a prophet who has appeared. So he spread his troops through the horizons, and sent nine of them from Yemen to Mecca. They came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was at Baṭn Nakhla, standing in prayer and reciting the Qur'an. It pleased them, their hearts softened towards it, and they became Muslim; and of their words is what Allah has related in this sura.
The readers are agreed on kasra in "إِنا" in His saying: ﴿فَقَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا قُرْآناً عَجَباً﴾, but they differed on what comes after that: they read وإنّا and وأَنَّا to the end of the sura, giving kasra to some and fatḥa to some.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAyyāsh, the brother of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, and Qays told me, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqama ibn Qays, that he read what is in [Sūrat] al-Jinn and al-Najm: (وأنا) with fatḥa. Al-Farrāʾ said: and Yaḥyā, Ibrāhīm and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh used to read it so. Nāfiʿ al-Madanī read with fatḥa, while al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and most of the people of Medina read with kasra, except that they read with fatḥa: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَسَاجِدَ للهِ﴾ (18). [Muḥammad told us, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Ḥibbān told me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: After the account of the jinn was related, there was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿وَأنَّ الْمَسَاجِدَ لِلهِ فَلاَ تَدْعُواْ﴾ (18).
ʿĀṣim used to read with kasra what was part of the jinn's speech, and with fatḥa what was part of the revelation. As for those who read all of them with fatḥa, they joined "أنَّ" back each time to His saying: فآمنا به — "and we believed in all of that" — so أن received fatḥa because "believing" acts upon it. Yet with that you find "believing" fits well in some of what has fatḥa and is awkward in others; but that does not prevent you from carrying them all through with fatḥa, for where an overt "we believed" is awkward, a verb akin to "believing" may fit well and require the fatḥa of أنَّ, as the Arabs said:
إذا ما الغانيات بَرَزْنَ يوماً * وزَجّجن الحَواجبَ والعُيونا
(When the fair women come out one day, having thinned their eyebrows and [darkened] their eyes.)
He put العيون in the accusative by making it follow الحواجب, although eyes are not thinned but only darkened with kohl; so he implied "kohl" for them. Likewise, in a place where آمنَّا (we believed) does not fit, one implies [a verb] that does fit: صدقنا (we affirmed), ألهمنا (we were inspired), شهدنا (we bore witness). The accusative reading is strengthened by His saying: ﴿وَأَنْ لَّوِ اسْتَقَامُوا عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ﴾ (16).
So whoever reads with kasra ought to drop (أنْ) from (لو), because (أنْ), when lightened, does not occur in quoted speech; do you not see that you say: أقول لو فعلتَ لفعلتُ (I say: had you done it, I would have done it), without introducing (أنْ)?
As for those who read all of them with kasra, they say in that case: ﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقَامُوا﴾ as though they implied an oath with لو and cut it off from the sequence joined to the beginning of the discourse, saying: والله أن لو استقاموا (by Allah, if they had kept straight). The Arabs put أن in this position with an oath, and also drop it. The poet said:
فأقسمُ لو شىء أتانا رسُوله * سواك، ولكن لم نجدْ لكَ مدفَعا
(I swear, had anything other than you sent us its messenger [we would have repelled it]; but we found no way to repel you.)
And another recited to me:
أمَا واللهِ أنْ لو كُنتَ حُرًّا * وما بِالحرِّ أنتَ ولا العتيقِ
(By Allah, if you were a free man — but you are neither free-born nor freed.)
Whoever reads all of them with kasra but reads ﴿وأن المساجد لله﴾ with fatḥa has singled it out as revelation, and has treated وأنْ لو as containing an implied oath, as I have described to you.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنَّا لاَ نَدْرِيۤ أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
This is from the speech of the unbelievers among the jinn; they said: We do not know whether this was done because good is intended for them or because of evil — meaning the pelting of the devils with the stars.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُنَّا طَرَآئِقَ قِدَداً﴾.
We were different sects, our inclinations differing. الطريقة is a man's way. It is also said [109/a] of a group: they are the طريقة of their people, when they are their leaders; and of one person too: [he is] the طريقة of his people. Likewise it is said of one person: this is the نظورة of his people, of the one whom they look up to; some of the Arabs say: نظيرة of his people; and both are pluralised نظائر.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن نُّعْجِزَ ٱللَّهَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
[I.e.] we knew with certainty.
One of the readers read: "أن لن تَقوَّل الإنسُ والجنُّ", but I will not name him.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلاَ يَخَافُ بَخْساً ﴾: nothing will be diminished from the reward of his deed, ﴿وَلاَ رَهَقاً﴾.
Nor wrong.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنَّا ٱلْقَاسِطُونَ﴾: they are the unjust, the unbelievers; and المقسطون are the just, the Muslims. And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَنْ أَسْلَمَ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ تَحَرَّوْاْ رَشَداً﴾.
He is saying: they made for guidance and followed it.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَلَّوِ ٱسْتَقَامُواْ عَلَى ٱلطَّرِيقَةِ﴾: on the way of unbelief, ﴿لأَسْقَيْنَاهُم مَّآءً غَدَقاً﴾ — it would be an increase in their wealth and their livestock. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿ولَوْلاَ أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَنْ يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمَنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفاً مِّن فِضَّةٍ﴾. He is saying: that is done to them so that it may be a trial for them in this world and an increase in the punishment of the Hereafter.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يُعْرِضْ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِ يَسْلُكْهُ عَذَاباً صَعَداً﴾.
It came down concerning al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī. They mention that الصَّعَد is a smooth rock in Hell which he is made to climb; when he reaches its top, he is thrown down into Hell, and that is his constant lot. Similar to it in Sūrat al-Muddaththir: ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُوداً﴾.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنَّ ٱلْمَسَاجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلاَ تَدْعُواْ﴾.
So do not associate with Him in them any idol or anything that is worshipped. It is said: [it means] these mosques. And it is said: وأن المساجد لله means a man's places of prostration: what he prostrates on — his forehead, his hands, his knees and the fronts of his feet.
[Translator's note: «يسحد» is as printed, for «يسجد».]

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ لَمَّا قَامَ عَبْدُ ٱللَّهِ يَدْعُوهُ﴾.
He means the Prophet ﷺ, on the night the jinn came to him at Baṭn Nakhla. ﴿كَادُواْ يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَداً﴾: they almost climbed on top of the Prophet ﷺ out of longing for the Qur'an and desire for it.
Some read: "لُبُدا", and the meaning of both — and Allah knows best — is one; one says لُبدَة and لِبدة.
Whoever reads "لُبَّداً" means to make it an adjective of men, as in your saying: رُكّعاً and ركوعا, سجَّدا and سجودا.

farraa:20-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَدْعُو رَبِّي﴾. Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read: "قُلْ إنما أدعُو ربِّى", and the generality of the people of Medina read likewise; some [read] (قال), and some (قل).
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said:] Muḥammad told us, he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl told me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — may Allah have mercy on him — that he read it: (قال إنما أَدْعُو رَبِّى).
The readers are agreed on ﴿لاَ أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرّاً﴾ with fatḥa on the ḍād; none of them read it with ḍamma.

farraa:22-22.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَنْ أَجِدَ مِن دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَداً﴾: a refuge, or a burrow in which I could take refuge.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ بَلاَغاً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِسَالاَتِهِ﴾.
It may be an exception from His saying: "I have no power to cause you harm or right guidance, except that I convey to you what I have been sent with".
There is another way in it: Say: none will protect me from Allah if I do not convey His message. Then the accusative of البلاغ is by an implied verb belonging to the conditional (jazāʾ), as you say to a man: إِلا قياماً فقعودا (if not standing, then sitting) and إلا عطاء فردا جميلا (if not a gift, then a gracious refusal), i.e. if you do not do [it], then [let it be] at least a gracious refusal. So لا is separate from إن [i.e. إلا = إنْ لا]. This is a good way. The Arabs say: إِن لا مال اليوم فلا مال أبدا (if there is no wealth today, there will be no wealth ever), treating (لا) as the lā of generic negation (tabriʾa); they also use the nominative with that meaning; and whoever uses the accusative with tanwīn does so by an implied verb. One of the Arabs recited to me:
فإن لا مَال أعطيه فإنى * صديق من غُدو أو رَواح
(If there is no wealth for me to give, then I am a friend, morning or evening.)

farraa:27-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ مَنِ ٱرْتَضَىٰ مِن رَّسُولٍ﴾.
For He acquaints him with [110/a] His unseen.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَسْلُكُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ رَصَداً﴾.
They mention that when Jibrīl ﷺ came down with the message to the Prophet ﷺ, angels from every heaven came down with him, guarding him against the jinn listening to the revelation in order to steal it and cast it to their soothsayers, so that they would anticipate the Prophet ﷺ with it. That is the guard before him and behind him. Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لِّيَعْلَمَ﴾, meaning Muḥammad ﷺ, ﴿أَن قَدْ أَبْلَغُواْ رِسَالاَتِ رَبِّهِمْ ﴾, meaning Jibrīl ﷺ. Some said: it is Muḥammad ﷺ, i.e.: Muḥammad knows that he has conveyed the message of his Lord.
Some read: "لِيُعْلَمَ أَنْ قَدْ أَبْلَغُوا", meaning: so that the jinn and mankind may know that the messengers have conveyed [the message], [and] not they [the jinn], with what they hoped for from eavesdropping.
[Translator's note: «لاهم» is as printed; it is read here as «لا هم» ("not they").]

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said:] Muḥammad told us, he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Abū Isrāʾīl told me, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, concerning His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا﴾; he said: the majesty of our Lord.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن تَقُولَ ٱلإِنسُ وَٱلْجِنُّ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً﴾.
ظن here means doubt.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَن يَسْتَمِعِ ٱلآنَ﴾: since Muḥammad ﷺ was sent, he finds for himself a meteor lying in wait, set in ambush for him to pelt him.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Jinn
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قُلْ أُوحِيَ إلَيَّ أنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِنَ الجِنِّ﴾ ("Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened"). The reading is «أُوحِيَ» with the wāw retained, and it has also been read «قُلْ أُحِيَ إلَيَّ» without wāw. Whoever says «أُحِيَ إلَيَّ», it is from «وَحَيْتُ إلَيْهِ», though «أوْحَيْتُ إلَيْهِ» is more common; the original is «وُحِيَ», but when the wāw takes a ḍamma, the hamza is sometimes substituted for it, as in ﴿وَإذا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 11] ("and when the messengers are given their appointed time"), whose original is «وُقِّتَتْ», because it is from «الوَقْت».
[Translator's note: the source prints the original form as «وَحِيَ»; the argument requires «وُحِيَ» (with ḍamma on the wāw).]
It has come in the exegesis that this group of the jinn listened to the Prophet ﷺ while he was praying the dawn prayer in Baṭn Nakhla, and that is His saying: ﴿وَإذْ صَرَفْنا إلَيْكَ نَفَرًا مِنَ الجِنِّ يَسْتَمِعُونَ القُرْآنَ فَلَمّا حَضَرُوهُ قالُوا أنْصِتُوا﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 29] ("And when We directed to you a group of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an; when they attended it, they said: Listen quietly"), i.e. some of them said to others: "Refrain from speaking and listen." It was said that they were of the jinn of Naṣībīn; it was said that they were from Yemen; it was said that they were Jews; and it was said that they were idolaters.
As for His saying ﴿أنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِنَ الجِنِّ﴾, «أنَّ» has fatḥa and nothing else. And His saying ﴿إنّا سَمِعْنا﴾ ("Indeed, we have heard"), His saying ﴿فَإنَّ لَهُ﴾ [al-Jinn: 23] ("then for him is…"), and His saying ﴿فَإنَّهُ يَسْلُكُ﴾ [al-Jinn: 27] ("then He dispatches") — these three have kasra and nothing else. The readers differed regarding the [occurrences] in this sura other than these three words: some of them said «وَأنَّهُ» and «وَأنّا» [with fatḥa]. As for ʿĀṣim, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated from him the like of the reading of Nāfiʿ and those who followed him, while Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān narrated from him the fatḥa where Abū Bakr read with kasra. What the grammarians choose is the reading of Nāfiʿ and those who followed him in this verse. According to them, whatever is construed as part of the revelation is «أنَّهُ» with fatḥa on «أنَّ», and whatever is the speech of the jinn has kasra, conjoined to His saying: ﴿فَقالُوا إنّا سَمِعْنا قُرْآنًا عَجَبًا﴾ ("and they said: Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an"). On this reading the meaning is: "And they said: Indeed, exalted is the majesty of our Lord", "and they said: Indeed, our foolish one used to say…".
As for whoever reads with fatḥa, some grammarians mentioned that it is conjoined to the hāʾ [in «بِهِ»], the meaning according to him being: "So we believed in it, and in that exalted is the majesty of our Lord", and likewise what comes after it, according to him. This is poor by analogy (qiyās): one does not conjoin to a genitive pronoun except by repeating the genitive-governing particle overtly. Rather, its proper analysis is that it is construed according to the meaning of «آمَنّا بِهِ» ("we believed in it"), because the meaning of «آمَنّا بِهِ» is "we affirmed it and knew it", so the meaning is: "and we affirmed that exalted is the majesty of our Lord."
[Translator's note: the source has «ورَوى حَفْصُ بْنُ سُلَيْمانَ عَنِ الفَتْحِ», which is translated here as "narrated from him the fatḥa".]

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَأنّا لا نَدْرِي أشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَن في الأرْضِ أمْ أرادَ بِهِمْ رَبُّهم رَشَدًا﴾ ("And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them right guidance"): the meaning is: "We do not know, with the occurrence of the pelting by the stars, whether there is good in that for the people of the earth or otherwise."

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿وَأنّا مِنّا الصّالِحُونَ ومِنّا دُونَ ذَلِكَ كُنّا طَرائِقَ قِدَدًا﴾ ("And among us are the righteous and among us are other than that; we were of divided ways"): «قِدَدًا» means "separated", i.e. we were separate groups, Muslims and non-Muslims.

zajjaj:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأنّا مِنّا المُسْلِمُونَ ومِنّا القاسِطُونَ﴾ ("And among us are the Muslims and among us are the unjust"): this is the explanation of their saying ﴿كُنّا طَرائِقَ قِدَدًا﴾ [al-Jinn: 11] ("we were of divided ways"). «القاسِطُون» are the unjust.
And His saying ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ تَحَرَّوْا رَشَدًا﴾ ("those have sought out right guidance"): He means they aimed at the path of truth and right guidance. I do not know of anyone who read «رُشْدًا» in this sura. «الرُّشْد» and «الرَّشَد» are both permissible in Arabic, except that the endings of the verses before and after «الرَّشَد» are with fatḥa, built on the pattern faʿal; so the verse-endings being on this form, and matching, is better. If a narration of reading it so is established, then reading it so is permissible; but it is not permissible to read with whatever is permissible in Arabic unless a narration and reading of it is established from an imam whose reading is followed — for following the reading is the Sunna, and seeking out anomalous (shādhdh) readings and reading by them is an innovation.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿وَأمّا القاسِطُونَ﴾ ("And as for the unjust"): one says «قَسَطَ الرَّجُلُ» when the man acts unjustly, and «أقْسَطَ» when he acts justly.

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿وَأنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا عَلى الطَّرِيقَةِ لأسْقَيْناهم ماءً غَدَقًا﴾ ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهم فِيهِ﴾ [al-Jinn: 17] ("And if they had kept straight on the way, We would have given them abundant water to drink, so that We might test them therein"). Its explanation is: "If they had kept straight on the way which is the way of guidance, We would have given them abundant water to drink." «الغَدَق» means abundant. The evidence for this explanation is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّ أهْلَ القُرى آمَنُوا واتَّقَوْا لَفَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ بَرَكاتٍ مِنَ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 96] ("And if the people of the towns had believed and feared Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth"), and like His saying: ﴿لأكَلُوا مِن فَوْقِهِمْ ومِن تَحْتِ أرْجُلِهِمْ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 66] ("they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet"). It has also been said that He means by it: "if they had kept straight on the way of unbelief"; the evidence for this explanation according to them is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَوْلا أنْ يَكُونَ النّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً لَجَعَلْنا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمَنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفًا مِن فِضَّةٍ ومَعارِجَ عَلَيْها يَظْهَرُونَ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 33] ("And were it not that mankind would become one community, We would have made for whoever disbelieves in the All-Merciful roofs of silver for their houses, and stairways upon which to mount"). What is chosen — and it is the majority of the exegesis — is that "the way" means the way of guidance, because «الطَّرِيقَة» is made definite with alif and lām, and what is most required is that it be the way of guidance, and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهم فِيهِ﴾ ("so that We might test them therein"): so that We might try them by that.
And His saying: ﴿وَمَن يُعْرِضْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِ يَسْلُكْهُ عَذابًا صَعَدًا﴾ ("And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, He will put him into a ṣaʿad punishment"): its meaning — and Allah knows best — is an arduous punishment. It was also said: a rock in Hell. In the language — and Allah knows best — it is an arduous course of punishment; one says «قَدْ وقَعَ القَوْمُ في صَعُودٍ وهَبُوطٍ» ("the people have fallen into ascents and descents") when they are on uneven ground and on an arduous path.
And it is read «لَأسْقَيْناهم ماءً غَدِقًا». «الغَدَق» is the maṣdar (verbal noun) and «الغَدِق» is the active participle; you say «غَدِقَ، يَغْدَقُ، غَدَقًا، فَهو غَدِقٌ» when moisture or water is abundant in a place.

zajjaj:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿وَأنَّ المَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أحَدًا﴾ ("And the places of prostration are for Allah, so do not invoke anyone along with Allah"): its meaning is the command to affirm the oneness of Allah in the prayers. It was also said: «المَساجِد» are the parts of a person on which prostration is made: the forehead, the nose, the two hands, the two knees and the two feet. «أنَّ» here may be in the position of an accusative, and may be in the position of a genitive; the meaning is: "Because the places of prostration are for Allah, do not invoke anyone along with Allah." When the lām was omitted, the position became an accusative position; and it may be genitive even though the lām does not appear, as the Arabs say «وَبَلَدٍ لَيْسَ بِهِ أنِيسٌ» ("and [many] a land in which there is no companion"), meaning «رُبَّ بَلَدٍ».

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿وَأنَّهُ لَمّا قامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ يَدْعُوهُ كادُوا يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَدًا﴾ ("And when the servant of Allah stood up invoking Him, they almost became about him a compacted mass"). It is also read «لُبَدًا», and «لُبَّدًا» is permissible. The meaning is that when the Prophet ﷺ prayed the dawn prayer at Dhāt Nakhla, the jinn — when they heard the Qur'an and marvelled at it — almost fell upon the Prophet ﷺ. It was also said: «كادُوا» ("they almost") refers to the whole assembly that banded together against the Prophet ﷺ. The meaning of «لُبَدًا» is: piled one upon another. Everything you stick firmly to something you have «لَبَدْتَهُ», and from this is the derivation of these felts (lubūd) that are spread out. Whoever reads «لِبَدًا», it is the plural of «لِبْدَة», [plural] «لِبَد»; whoever reads «لُبَدًا», it is the plural of «لُبْدَة», [plural] «لُبَد»; «لُبْدَة» and «لِبْدَة» have one meaning. And the meaning for whoever reads «لُبَّدًا»: it is the plural of «لابِد», [plural] «لُبَّد», like «راكِع» and «رُكَّع», «غازٍ» and «غُزًّى».

zajjaj:22-22.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَنْ أجِدَ مِن دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَدًا﴾ ("and I will never find besides Him a refuge"), i.e. a place of escape, except that its derivation is from «اللَّحْد» (the niche of a grave). It is like ﴿لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَأً أوْ مَغاراتٍ أوْ مُدَّخَلا﴾ [al-Tawba: 57] ("If they could find a refuge, or caves, or a place to enter"); so «المُلْتَحَد» is of the same kind as «المُدَّخَل». The accusative of ﴿إلا بَلاغًا﴾ [al-Jinn: 23] ("except a conveyance [of the message]") is as a badal (substitute) for His saying ﴿مُلْتَحَدًا﴾; the meaning is: "I will never find besides Him a place of escape, except conveying", i.e. nothing will save me except that I convey from Allah what I have been sent with.

zajjaj:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿أمْ يَجْعَلُ لَهُ رَبِّي أمَدًا﴾ ("or whether my Lord will appoint for it a distant term"), i.e. a remoteness, as He said: ﴿قُلْ إنْ أدْرِي أقَرِيبٌ ما تُوعَدُونَ﴾ ("Say: I do not know whether what you are promised is near").

zajjaj:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿عالِمُ الغَيْبِ فَلا يُظْهِرُ عَلى غَيْبِهِ أحَدًا﴾ ﴿إلا مَنِ ارْتَضى مِن رَسُولٍ﴾ [al-Jinn: 27] ("[He is] the Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to whom He has approved of messengers"). This verse entails, regarding anyone who claims that the stars guide him to what will happen of life and death and other things, that he has disbelieved in what is in the Qur'an; and likewise His saying: ﴿قُلْ لا يَعْلَمُ مَن في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ الغَيْبَ إلا اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Naml: 65] ("Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah"). The exception in His saying ﴿إلا مَنِ ارْتَضى مِن رَسُولٍ﴾ [al-Jinn: 27] means that He discloses His unseen only to the messengers, because the prophethood of the messengers is proved by miraculous signs and by their informing of the unseen, so that by this it is known that they differ from those who are not prophets. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He guards that, in that ﴿يَسْلُكُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ ومِن خَلْفِهِ رَصَدًا﴾ [al-Jinn: 27] ("He dispatches before him and behind him guardians"): when the angel descends with revelation, Allah sends guardians with him who protect the angel lest one of the jinn come and overhear the revelation and inform the soothsayers of it, and they inform people of it and so become equal to the prophets. So Allah made known that He dispatches guardians before the angel and behind him.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿لِيَعْلَمَ أنْ قَدْ أبْلَغُوا رِسالاتِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ ("that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord"). It may be [the sense] that the Prophet ﷺ may know that the message came to him and did not reach anyone else; and it may be — and Allah knows best — that Allah may know that they have conveyed His messages, and what comes after it indicates this, namely His saying: ﴿وَأحاطَ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ وأحْصى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَدًا﴾ ("and He has encompassed whatever is with them and has enumerated all things in number"); for this pronoun latent in ﴿وَأحْصى﴾ refers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to no one else.
﴿عَدَدًا﴾ is accusative in two ways: on the meaning "He has enumerated everything in the state of number" [i.e. as a ḥāl], so that neither the fall of a leaf nor a grain in the darkness of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, is hidden from Him; and it is possible that ﴿عَدَدًا﴾ is in the position of a maṣdar (verbal noun) construed according to the meaning of «وَأحْصى», because the meaning of «أحْصى» is "He counted everything in number (ʿadda kulla shayʾin ʿadadan)".

zajjaj:3-3.t: The interpretation of ﴿تَعالى جَدُّ رَبِّنا﴾ ("exalted is the jadd of our Lord") is: "Exalted are the majesty and greatness of our Lord above taking a consort or a child."

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَأنَّهُ كانَ رِجالٌ مِنَ الإنْسِ يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجالٍ مِنَ الجِنِّ فَزادُوهم رَهَقًا﴾ ("And there were men from mankind who sought refuge in men from the jinn, so they increased them in rahaq"). When a group of the people of the Jāhiliyya passed by a valley, they used to say: "We seek refuge in the mighty one of this valley from the rebellious and foolish among the jinn." The meaning of ﴿فَزادُوهم رَهَقًا﴾ is: they increased them in abasement and weakness. It is possible — and Allah knows best — that the humans who used to seek refuge in the jinn increased the jinn in rahaq, and it is possible that the jinn increased the humans in rahaq.

zajjaj:8-9.t: His saying: ﴿وَأنّا لَمَسْنا السَّماءَ فَوَجَدْناها مُلِئَتْ حَرَسًا شَدِيدًا وشُهُبًا﴾ ﴿وَأنّا كُنّا نَقْعُدُ مِنها مَقاعِدَ لِلسَّمْعِ فَمَن يَسْتَمِعِ الآنَ يَجِدْ لَهُ شِهابًا رَصَدًا﴾ ("And we sought the heaven and found it filled with stern guards and flaming stars; and we used to sit in positions therein to listen, but whoever listens now will find a flaming star lying in wait for him"), i.e. we used to listen, but now, when we tried to listen, we were pelted with the flaming stars, which are the stars. ﴿رَصَدًا﴾ means: guardians who prevent listening. It was said that the shooting down with which the devils were pelted arose after the sending of the Prophet (peace be upon him), and it is one of his signs.
